section_summary: This section covers Japanese wartime taxation, inflation, bond financing, and draft financial rules for a prospective U.S. military government. It also records American and British bondholders’ efforts to establish claims on Japanese debt, Japanese postwar financial measures, and their effect on foreign nationals.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on Japan’s 1945–1946 budget estimates
subfiles.about: Points to an original item concerning Japanese budget estimates.
subfiles.summary: Refers readers to another file for Japan’s 1945–1946 budget estimates.

subfiles.title: Japanese financing of the war
subfiles.from: J. Klahr Huddle, U.S. Legation, Bern
subfiles.about: Transmits a German newspaper report on Japan’s proposed supplementary tax law.
subfiles.summary: Reports anticipated increases in income, alcohol, entertainment, and railway ticket taxes.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Financing of the War
subfiles.about: Explains a proposed Japanese tax law intended to finance the war and reduce purchasing power.
subfiles.summary: Details higher personal and corporate income taxes and proposed indirect taxes, while questioning the revenue likely from rationed alcohol and entertainment.

subfiles.title: Financial directive for military government in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests comments or approval on a draft financial directive.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Civil Affairs Division draft for concurrence.

subfiles.title: Draft financial directive for military government in Japan
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: Director of European Affairs, State Department
subfiles.about: Sends a draft occupation financial directive for concurrence.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the January 19 draft financial directive.

subfiles.title: Financial Directive for Military Government in Japan
subfiles.about: Sets proposed currency and financial rules for occupation forces.
subfiles.summary: The draft provides for supplemental military yen and regular yen, restricts dollar circulation and foreign exchange, and establishes records of currency use. It calls for blocking specified assets, supervising banks, and controlling currency issues and securities transactions.

subfiles.title: Financial Directive for Military Government in Japan, duplicate
subfiles.about: Duplicates the proposed occupation financial directive.
subfiles.summary: A second, poorly reproduced copy repeats the provisions on military yen, dollar use, financial records, blocked assets, and bank supervision.

subfiles.title: Inflation in Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a condensed translation of a Japanese article on inflation.
subfiles.summary: Highlights rising note circulation and unsubscribed bonds held by the Bank of Japan.

subfiles.title: Basic accounting instructions for military government in Japan
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Sends draft accounting instructions for comment.
subfiles.summary: Encloses instructions supplementing the financial directive.

subfiles.title: Basic Accounting Instructions
subfiles.about: Prescribes accounting for occupation currencies, expenditures, assets, and civilian supplies.
subfiles.summary: The instructions centralize yen accounting and require receipts for advances to military disbursing officers. They distinguish expenses charged to U.S. appropriations from other yen expenditures and call for audits, regular financial reports, and records of civilian supplies.

subfiles.title: Inflation in Japan, duplicate despatch
subfiles.about: Repeats the cover despatch transmitting an article on Japanese inflation.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the despatch on note circulation and unsubscribed bonds.

subfiles.title: Inflation
subfiles.from: Toyo Keizai; translated by American Coordinated Translation Center
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japanese note inflation and the government bond market.
subfiles.summary: Reports a 92 percent annual rise in Bank of Japan note circulation, large holdings of unsubscribed bonds, and increased bank lending to support bond subscriptions. It urges tighter control of government spending and fairer income distribution.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on Norwegian government bonds
subfiles.about: Points to information on two new Norwegian government bond series.
subfiles.summary: Directs readers to the original Bern report on Norwegian bonds.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning Japanese and German bonds
subfiles.about: Forwards Senator Wiley’s constituent inquiry concerning enemy bonds.
subfiles.summary: Sends the Woods correspondence and Treasury’s reply because the inquiry concerns claims.

subfiles.title: Woods inquiry about Japanese and German bonds
subfiles.about: Asks Treasury to report on a constituent’s bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Charles R. Woods’s correspondence and requests a reply in duplicate.

subfiles.title: Japanese and German bonds in the Woods estate
subfiles.about: Asks about claims against enemy assets and access to a list of American enemy-bond holders.
subfiles.summary: Seeks help with roughly $35,000 in inherited Japanese and German bonds.

subfiles.title: Proposed use of German assets to pay bondholders
subfiles.about: Replies to a proposal to pay enemy bonds from German assets in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Says congressional policy is unsettled and available assets fall short of competing claims.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply on Woods’s bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Explains Treasury’s claims procedures and limits on disclosure of property census reports.
subfiles.summary: Treasury has no blocked-property claims procedure or compiled bondholder list and keeps census reports confidential.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Woods’s bonds
subfiles.about: Explains how Woods may place information about inherited enemy bonds on record.
subfiles.summary: The Department cannot pursue claims with enemy governments and does not ordinarily intervene for purchasers of foreign government bonds. It invites detailed bond, ownership, interest-payment, and citizenship information for possible postwar consideration.

subfiles.title: Copy of State Department reply to Wiley
subfiles.about: Transmits State’s response to Senator Wiley.
subfiles.summary: Sends Treasury a copy of the reply about Woods’s bonds.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on bank consolidation
subfiles.about: Points to a report on consolidation of banks in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes that nine large banks in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya were reportedly to be consolidated.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on J. T. Ruche’s investments
subfiles.about: Points to correspondence about investments in Germany and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Refers to J. T. Ruche’s inquiry about recovering his investments.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note to Clayton
subfiles.about: Calls attention to a conversation involving Treasury Secretary Morgenthau.
subfiles.summary: Asks Clayton to note the reported conversation; much of the handwriting is unclear.

subfiles.title: Directive on Japan
subfiles.about: Records Morgenthau’s request for Treasury involvement in drafting the Japan directive.
subfiles.summary: Morgenthau objects to Treasury’s exclusion from the draft occupation directive. Grew says the text remains unsettled and promises Treasury an opportunity to review it.

subfiles.title: Woods letter concerning bond claims and frozen funds
subfiles.about: Presses for action on inherited enemy bonds and possible payment from frozen assets.
subfiles.summary: The difficult-to-read letter follows up on State’s March reply and urges consideration of bondholders’ claims against enemy funds.

subfiles.title: Woods letter to Senator Wiley
subfiles.about: Requests help obtaining relief for inherited Japanese and German bonds.
subfiles.summary: Woods seeks claims against frozen assets, overdue interest, and contact with other bondholders.

subfiles.title: Phil A. Woods’s share of the F. R. Woods estate
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese and German bonds allotted to Phil A. Woods.
subfiles.summary: Records bond issues, serial numbers, purchase prices, maturities, and unpaid coupons.

subfiles.title: Charles R. Woods’s share of the F. R. Woods estate
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese and German bonds allotted to Charles R. Woods.
subfiles.summary: Records Oriental Development, Dawes Loan, and Young Loan holdings with serial numbers and defaulted coupons.

subfiles.title: Answer to State Department form letter
subfiles.about: Supplies ownership and acquisition details for the estate’s bonds.
subfiles.summary: States the bonds were bought in the United States, held there, and had unpaid interest.

subfiles.title: Wiley forwards Woods’s renewed bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards Woods’s letters and bond information.
subfiles.summary: Requests a report in duplicate for transmission to Woods.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Woods’s renewed inquiry
subfiles.about: Responds to Woods’s documentation and proposal to use frozen funds.
subfiles.summary: State has recorded Woods’s information but cannot predict treatment of the bonds in a peace settlement. It refers his frozen-funds proposal to Treasury and returns his originals.

subfiles.title: Woods correspondence forwarded to Treasury
subfiles.about: Sends Woods’s comments on paying bonds from frozen funds.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Woods’s letters and State’s reply for Treasury’s consideration.

subfiles.title: Comments on financial directive for Japan
subfiles.about: Comments on proposed occupation financial controls.
subfiles.summary: Questions inconsistent treatment of banknotes and bank offices, broad blocking of government and Imperial Household assets, treatment of Shinto funds, and staffing for enforcement.

subfiles.title: Reply to Christensen on Japanese bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds to an inquiry about Japanese government and Yokohama bonds.
subfiles.summary: Explains State’s general approach to foreign bond defaults, suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and says the peace settlement’s treatment of such obligations remains unknown.

subfiles.title: Christensen asks about Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Requests information on the fate of his Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Asks for a brief assessment of approximately $2,000 in bonds.

subfiles.title: Views of Finance Minister Shibusawa
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits an interview on Japanese war-contract compensation and taxation.
subfiles.summary: Reports Finance Minister Shibusawa’s views on cancelling compensation to war industries and taxing wartime wealth, alongside estimates of substantial payments to major producers.

subfiles.title: Interview with Finance Minister Shibusawa
subfiles.about: Discusses proposals to cancel war-contract compensation and impose taxes on wartime gains.
subfiles.summary: The poorly reproduced interview weighs the effect of cancelling promised payments on industrial firms and describes possible taxes on wealth or property. Shibusawa also discusses inflation, production, and the distribution of postwar financial burdens.

subfiles.title: Christensen acknowledges bond reply
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Department’s reply on Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Corliss and says the explanation of State’s position was clear.

subfiles.title: Law for the Establishment of the Foreign Trade Fund
subfiles.about: Transmits Japan’s newly promulgated Foreign Trade Fund law.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the law passed by the 89th Imperial Diet.

subfiles.title: Law for the Establishment of the Foreign Trade Fund
subfiles.about: Establishes a government fund for foreign-trade transactions.
subfiles.summary: The law sets aside ¥50 million, permits temporary borrowing when necessary, and authorizes use of the fund for trade goods and foreign currency. It assigns fund operations to the Bank of Japan under the finance minister’s direction.

subfiles.title: British debate over Japanese loan payments
subfiles.about: Reports British parliamentary remarks and press criticism concerning Japanese bond payments.
subfiles.summary: Chancellor Dalton suggests that wartime claims outrank prewar Japanese bondholders. The Times disputes his remarks and stresses that many loans were issued when Japan was a British ally.

subfiles.title: Financial press protests over Dalton’s Japanese bond remarks
subfiles.about: Reports market reaction and editorials about British treatment of Japanese loans.
subfiles.summary: Financial newspapers report falling Japanese bond prices and broader uncertainty in foreign bonds after Dalton’s statement. Commentators argue for protecting prewar holders and debate whether reparations should take priority over private claims.

subfiles.title: British protests over Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Reports organized bond-market protests and commentary on Dalton’s position.
subfiles.summary: Investment groups protest Dalton’s remarks. Financial commentator Paul Einzig suggests Dalton favors reparations over prewar bond claims, though his broader position on foreign loans may differ.

subfiles.title: Dalton’s further answers on Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Reports Dalton’s further parliamentary answers.
subfiles.summary: Dalton says he will discuss Japanese bonds with bondholder, investment-trust, and insurance representatives.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for despatch no. 393
subfiles.about: Routes the following despatch for action and information.
subfiles.summary: Lists offices receiving despatch no. 393.

subfiles.title: Application of Emergency Financial Measures and Proposed Tax Laws to Foreign Nationals
subfiles.about: Reports how Japanese emergency financial rules affect foreign nationals and diplomats.
subfiles.summary: Long-term foreign residents generally fall under Japanese deposit and currency restrictions, while accredited diplomats and certain later entrants receive exemptions. The application of proposed taxes and a capital levy to foreigners remains undecided.

subfiles.title: Yokohama inquiry on currency restrictions
subfiles.about: Asks whether American residents are subject to Japanese currency and deposit restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Seeks guidance to answer Americans concerned about low monthly withdrawal allowances.

subfiles.title: Freezing regulations applied to American citizens
subfiles.about: Clarifies which foreign residents are subject to emergency financial rules.
subfiles.summary: Long-term private residents are generally covered; qualifying later Allied and neutral entrants receive military-equivalent privileges.

subfiles.title: Questions on foreign funds, taxes, and capital levy
subfiles.about: Conveys Swiss and British questions about restrictions on foreign funds and firms.
subfiles.summary: Asks about diplomatic funds, foreign residents’ allowances, and tax or levy exemptions.

subfiles.title: Exemption of Certain Categories of Funds from Blocking
subfiles.about: States exemptions from Japanese deposit blocking.
subfiles.summary: Official Allied and neutral funds and accredited diplomats’ personal funds are exempt; tax and levy treatment remains undecided.

subfiles.title: Green inquiry on Japanese government bonds
subfiles.about: Asks about Japanese dollar bonds due in 1954.
subfiles.summary: Seeks guidance on bonds he holds following a Department announcement.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Green
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains the Department’s position on Green’s Japanese dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that an August press release concerned equity interests, not government bonds. State cannot yet predict the bonds’ treatment in a peace settlement, suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and offers to record Green’s holdings.

subfiles.title: Green follow-up on Japanese bonds
subfiles.to: Division of Financial Affairs, State Department
subfiles.about: Raises further questions about Imperial Japanese bonds due in 1954.
subfiles.summary: The partially legible letter concerns Green’s holdings and their possible value.
